item.title: Novote
item.content:encoded: I found it to be an above average article. Conceptually, a humanoid what cures diseases is usually as uncreative as you can get, but this article managed to give him an actual personality, so it gets a pass in my book. The gay subplot was pretty gay (jk) was pretty cool, and I liked that the doctor was able to quickly grasp that homosexuality isn't a personality or brain disorder. However, I don't like this flowery belief that mental illness is somehow leagues more difficult than physical illness. Perhaps this is just me, but I don't mental illness particularly harder to deal with than physical ones. It's only because we lack a lot of information regarding our brains currently that causes such a big divide between the two.

item.content:encoded:
I like this, and the relationship between Dr Bridge and 948 develops well, but there are a few things I didn't follow:

  • Does 948 realise that he anomalously cures people? The final log suggests not, but in that case, how does he react when people bring patients into his lecture? Surely that's seen as disruptive.
  • If 948 doesn't acknowledge his anomalous properties, how has the Foundation tested the cures? Do they hear him start a new topic on chemotherapy, and think "yikes, let's go find a cancer patient"? How was the healing effect discovered in the first place, in that case?
  • Why does the Foundation leave 948 in the lecture theatre? Surely containment would be easier in a Foundation site, not a public building - notwithstanding that he becomes "extremely aggravated" - the Foundation contains much more hostile/dangerous humanoids.
  • If 948 has been lecturing continuously, when did he find the time to read the new textbooks?

I also wonder whether you could squeeze in one more feel in relation to Dr Bridge's request in the last log. 948's statement "You don't fix anger and heartbreak like you fix muscle and sinew" isn't particularly medical. Surely it's just as relevant that there is no current "medical procedure" he could discuss that would allow for the increased uptake of the relevant neurotransmitters in Dr Bridge's head. Just like in 1984, there was no medical procedure he could have lectured about to help Cillian - although if Cillian had lived a little longer, then there would have been…

item.title: Deep, moving and compelling! A very human piece in an Internet full of isolated plastic and Creepypasta!
item.content:encoded:
I can't say enough about it.

  • It speaks of the human experience through many relatable elements
  • The drama and sub-text within the SCP tells multiple stories at once. Great stuff!
  • Portrays the Foundation as an organization comprised of living, breathing people. A breath of fresh air in a web filled with horror (and other) stories which seem somewhat if not completely inaccessible from the other ide of the screen!
  • Even in lieu of his isolation from others for sociological and practical reasons, SCP-948 seems not only unaware of his own nature as an extraordinary human being (anomaly would objectify him too much)
  • Deep, moving and compelling!

I can't really add any negatives at this point. I would have to work to find something wrong with it. It's one of those pieces where I'd rather leave it as it stands then to attempt to go through it with a fine comb and contrive improvements. I find that to be too arduous and consuming, anyway, and I often find it hard to articulate such things.

Definitely a +vote !

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I first read 948 back in 2013 or 2014, before I was a site member. I didn't like it, exactly, but something about it stuck with me for ages. The desperation, the frustration of stifled communication, that central question of what it means to 'cure' mental illness. When I saw it in deletion threshold a week or so ago, all that came rushing back, and it felt right to see how I could tackle those parts of it that had meant something to me, charge them with my own particular perspective.

In my own writing, I priotitise the themes and emotions I want to explore much more than the framing of those ideas, and I decided early on that it was right to treat this rewrite in the same way. Some might disagree, but that feels more respectful to me. Long story short, that meant dialogue, and that meant a humanoid. Ultimately, I hope that I retained the soul of the original, despite the recontextualisation.

A bunch of thanks are in order for this - to Dex for supporting this more abstract take and working with me to make it happen, to the many many people who gave crit on this1, to my parents for inspiring certain elements, to the Rewrite team for talking me through the process and being open about their thoughts on it. Thanks, as always, to AidenEldritch for being a fucking dork.

I hope you enjoyed!

Footnotes
1. I'm so sorry I didn't take note of all of you, and it feels wrong to only name a few.

item.title: Spiritual Successor.
item.content:encoded:
This began as a rewrite of the old SCP-948, “HOPE”, a hospital which allowed one within its walls to recover their mental scars and illnesses. It was rewritten to be as such by me back in 2010, with minor edits here and there until about 2014.

The original SCP was ported over from the old site by Far2, and was an orphaned article, as many Old Site relics are. With its rewrite, I became sole owner of the article.

Recently 948 fell below -10 and Rimple came up to rewrite it. He came up with the current draft - I’m a pretty big fan of it, as it keeps the basest essence of the idea, while going in a much more modern direction. It’s not perfect, no, but I like its direction.

The Rewrite Team decided that Rimples new draft here is not close enough to SCP-948 “Hope” as it was to count as a proper rewrite, so we reached a compromise. I deleted the old article, keeping a draft on Google Docs of both my most recent interpretation, and the oldest possible draft ported over by Far2. Rimple’s article here takes the slot as a spiritual successor.

It’s unorthodox, but the Rewrite team was more or less on board, and suggested this course of action.

NOW, WITHOUT FURTHER ADO, please enjoy Rimple's article here. In the future, I shall redo SCP-948 “Hope” as a hospital again, but not here. Needs to see a rebirth, not a rewrite.

It's all Rimple's now.
